title: Evaluate RAG Answer Quality
description: A small playbook for checking answer quality, evidence use, and retrieval fit.
text:
Evaluate RAG Answer Quality 
 Use this playbook when a RAG prototype starts producing plausible answers and needs a disciplined quality check. 
 Steps 
  Create 20 representative questions with expected evidence.  Log retrieved chunks, final answer, citations, and latency.  Score retrieval relevance before scoring the answer.  Mark answer failures as missing evidence, wrong evidence, bad synthesis, or unsafe response.  Promote recurring failures into regression tests.  
 Output 
 Produce a short eval note with pass rate, failure clusters, examples, and the next change to test.

title: Mental Models for AI Systems
description: A compact set of mental models for thinking about AI systems beyond model demos.
text:
Mental Models for AI Systems 
 An AI system is a loop: inputs, model behavior, product constraints, evaluation signals, and human feedback. The model is important, but it is not the whole system. 
 Useful Frames 
   Model as component:  treat the model as one fallible service in a larger product.   Distribution shift:  ask what changes between the examples you test and the users you serve.   Error budget:  decide which failures are tolerable, visible, recoverable, or unacceptable.  
 Link Forward 
 Use this note before designing  RAG First-Pass Design  or writing an evaluation playbook.

title: Transformer Attention Map
description: A short conceptual note on attention as routing over token representations.
text:
Transformer Attention Map 
 Attention lets a token representation read from other token representations. It is not magic memory; it is a learned routing pattern over the current context. 
 Why It Matters 
  It explains why context order and formatting affect model behavior.  It helps separate retrieval problems from reasoning or instruction problems.  It gives a mental model for context limits, compression, and prompt structure.  
 Practical Check 
 When an LLM ignores a detail, ask whether the detail was visible, salient, and connected to the task. Then test with a smaller, sharper context before changing models.

title: Must Know
description: The smallest useful vocabulary for reading and building AI systems.
text:
Must Know 
 The minimum useful AI vocabulary is not a list of tools. It is a set of distinctions that prevent fuzzy thinking. 
 Baseline Distinctions 
  A model is not the product; it is one component in a system.  A prompt is an interface, not a substitute for product design.  Evaluation is not a final gate; it is an operating loop.  Retrieval improves grounding only when the index, ranking, and citation path are designed.  Safety and security are design constraints, not cleanup tasks.

Phase 00 Orientation 
 The goal of orientation is to know where you are in the map: concept, model behavior, engineering surface, evaluation, or operating practice. 
 Outcomes

title: RAG First-Pass Design
description: A small checklist for designing a first useful RAG system.
text:
RAG First-Pass Design 
 A first-pass RAG system should optimize for inspectability before cleverness. If you cannot explain where an answer came from, you cannot evaluate it. 
 Minimum Design 
  Define the answerable question set.  Choose source documents and ownership rules.  Pick chunk boundaries that preserve meaning.  Store citations with retrieved chunks.  Evaluate retrieval separately from final answer quality.  
 Failure Signals 
 Watch for correct-looking answers with missing citations, retrieval hits that are semantically close but task-irrelevant, and prompts that hide evidence instead of exposing it.

title: Start Here

text:
Start Here 
 AI Atlas is a personal working map, not a complete textbook. Start by building vocabulary, then connect concepts to repeatable engineering practice. 
 How to Use This Atlas 
  Read the phase pages in order.  Skim branch indexes before diving into individual notes.  Use playbooks when a concept needs to become a procedure.  Keep references in registries so atomic notes stay compact.  
 First Loop 
 Start with  Must Know , then read  Mental Models for AI Systems  and  Transformer Attention Map .
